governing_question: can fresh broker / reset semantics be made correct without silently falling back to a raw path string?
answer: YES — but only with a freshly-constructed broker per reader invocation. A single reused broker object is provably unsafe.

chunk_mechanism.source: pyreadstat.read_file_in_chunks RE-INVOKES the read function once per chunk
chunk_mechanism.loop_verbatim: while len(df): df, meta = read_function(file_path, row_offset=offset, row_limit=chunksize, **kwargs); offset += chunksize
chunk_mechanism.plus: it also performs a `metadataonly=True` call on the same file_path before the loop
chunk_mechanism.consequence: the same file object is handed to ReadStat repeatedly; its position is NOT reset between invocations

chunked_via_single_broker_object.result: FAILED — ReadstatError: 'This version of the file format is not supported'
chunked_via_single_broker_object.cause: the first metadata read advanced the broker toward EOF; the next invocation began mid-stream

fresh_broker_per_call.call: for off in (0,200,400): read_dta(fresh_broker, row_offset=off, row_limit=200)
fresh_broker_per_call.significance: a fresh broker per invocation yields correct chunk semantics AND complete per-invocation read/byte accounting at one app-owned seam

reuse_hazard.call: two consecutive read_dta calls on the SAME broker
reuse_hazard.second_call_result: FAILED — ReadstatError: 'This version of the file format is not supported'

bservation_on_escapes.so_today: every reader invocation is a RAW PATH STRING — the broker route is not in use at all yet
bservation_on_escapes.required_change: replace str(source) with a freshly-constructed governed broker at EACH of the three reader invocations (metadata probe, compatibility full read, chunked route)

row_limit_effect.finding: row_limit DOES reduce observed bytes (500 rows -> 555 reads/9825 bytes; row_limit=10 -> 65 reads/1985 bytes)
row_limit_effect.contrast: usecols does NOT reduce observed bytes (see 02/A5)
row_limit_effect.significance: the seam gives real I/O observability for ROW bounding but NOT column bounding — reinforcing that usecols is a projection, not a physical read restriction

safe_design_law: one app-owned open per reader invocation, wrapped in a broker that records read count and bytes and enforces the frozen budget
always construct a FRESH broker for each pyreadstat read call — never reuse an object across invocations
enforce ceilings by returning a premature EOF (b'') — NEVER by raising inside read() (raising hangs the reader; see 02)
keep the path string out of the reader call entirely so the compiled open handler stays a no-op
residual: this review established the reset law on synthetic carriers at the R7 grain. The claim that EVERY relevant reader call site can be brokered with no raw path-string escape remains an IMPLEMENTATION-lane proof (three call sites identified in the freeze decoder; all three are currently raw paths).
